job.title: Chief Executive Officer - arbias
job.description:
Chief Executive Officer


  • Lead a respected and trusted for-purpose organisation across Vic & NSW
  • Shape the next chapter of growth, impact and sustainability
  • Partner with an engaged Board to deliver strategy and strengthen impact



About arbias


Established in 1990, arbias Ltd is a not-for-profit organisation and recognised industry leader in Acquired Brain Injury (ABI) and complex needs, delivering specialist services across metropolitan, rural and regional communities in Victoria and New South Wales.


arbias supports people living with suspected or diagnosed ABI, as well as people with multiple and complex needs that may include physical disability, mental health challenges, alcohol and other drug-related issues and involvement with the criminal justice system. Its multidisciplinary team works alongside individuals to build independence, strengthen life skills, reconnect with community and navigate everyday life through compassionate, evidence-based and person-centred support.


With a workforce of more than 100 employees, arbias delivers services through a range of funding pathways including the NDIS and TAC. Its work spans direct service delivery, neuropsychological and specialist clinical services, community programs, training, research and advocacy, with services extending across Victoria and New South Wales.


arbias enters its next chapter from a position of specialist strength and established reputation. The organisation is focused on managing the transition from long-standing leadership with care, strengthening sustainability and external relationships, and pursuing considered growth while protecting the service quality and person-centred approach that have defined arbias for more than three decades.

 

 

 

About the role

Reporting to the Board, the Chief Executive Officer will provide the strategic, financial, operational and cultural leadership of arbias. The CEO will guide the transition from long-standing leadership, maintaining stability and trust while establishing a clear direction for the organisation's next phase.


In constructive partnership with the Board, the CEO will execute strategy, strengthen financial sustainability and navigate the government funding, tendering and NDIS environment. The role oversees performance, service quality, workforce capability, risk and compliance, supported by transparent, timely and 'no surprises' governance.


The CEO will strengthen senior relationships across government, funding and commissioning bodies, community organisations and sector partners. As a credible representative and advocate, they will build the visibility, influence and partnerships needed to create opportunities for arbias and the people it supports.


Internally, the CEO will be accessible and visible across a geographically dispersed workforce, developing the executive team and sustaining employee engagement through transition. They will foster an inclusive, collaborative and accountable culture while pursuing growth that builds on arbias' specialist strengths and protects service quality.


 

About You


You are a values-led senior executive with the breadth, judgement and resilience to lead a complex, government-funded service organisation. You may be an experienced CEO or a senior executive ready to step into a CEO role, bringing demonstrated success leading people and operations, strengthening organisational capability and maintaining an engaged workforce through change.


You combine strategic thinking with strong commercial and financial judgement. You understand how to build a sustainable operating model, navigate funding and commissioning arrangements and tenders, manage risk and translate strategy into disciplined organisational performance - without losing sight of service quality, client outcomes or purpose.


You are also a highly credible relationship builder and communicator, able to engage confidently with Boards, government, funders, employees, clients, families and sector partners. You will bring an open and constructive approach to governance, provide clear advice and appropriate challenge, and build trusted relationships that strengthen arbias' profile and influence.


Experience in disability and community services, health and human services, justice and corrections, government or another purpose-driven, stakeholder-rich environment will be relevant. Direct experience in ABI, disability or NDIS-funded services will be highly regarded but is not essential. Most important will be your empathy, curiosity and genuine commitment to human rights, inclusion and equitable outcomes, together with the capacity to understand and protect arbias' specialist purpose. Lived experience of disability would be valued.


 

Additional Requirements


The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to arbias’ vision, mission, objectives and organisational values. Eligibility to work in Australia, a current National Police Check, Australian driver licence and NDIS Worker Screening clearance are required. The role requires regular travel across Victoria and New South Wales, including rural and regional locations, and flexibility to work outside standard hours when required.


 

Application Details


Hazel Executive & Boards is pleased to be partnering with the arbias Board on the search and appointment of its next Chief Executive Officer. This appointment is being conducted through a confidential executive search process, supported by targeted market engagement and advertising.

job.title: Deputy Secretary, Strategy and Portfolio Performance
job.description:
Deputy Secretary, Strategy and Portfolio Performance


  • Shape DGS's enterprise strategy and future direction
  • Guide portfolio direction, prioritisation, sequencing and investment discipline
  • Advise the Secretary and strengthen whole-of-department performance

 


About Department of Government Services


The Department of Government Services (DGS) was established on 1 January 2023 to improve how Victorians and businesses experience government. DGS brings together important day-to-day services and is focused on making government easier, more connected and more seamless.


Its diverse portfolio includes citizen-facing services, digital platforms, regulatory functions and enterprise services, including Service Victoria, Consumer Affairs Victoria, Births, Deaths and Marriages Victoria, Local Government Victoria, Public Record Office Victoria, cyber security, procurement and grants-related functions.


DGS plays a central role in shaping how government services are designed, delivered and experienced across Victoria. It is connecting and digitising systems and platforms across state and local government while strengthening corporate and procurement services across the Victorian Public Sector.

 

About the role


The Deputy Secretary, Strategy and Portfolio Performance is a key enterprise leadership role reporting to the Secretary. The role leads DGS's enterprise strategy and portfolio performance function and supports the Secretary and Executive Board to make coherent decisions about the department's portfolio direction, priorities, sequencing, performance and future direction.


Working in partnership with portfolio Deputy Secretaries as outcome owners, the role translates government, customer and departmental priorities into clear portfolio direction, prioritisation, sequencing and disciplined investment choices. It brings together enterprise strategy, service and product portfolio lifecycle stewardship, customer insight, integrated planning and performance.


The role will guide difficult choices about what DGS should accelerate, sequence, reshape, pause or stop, including how services and products should evolve over time as part of an interconnected portfolio. It will balance public value and customer outcomes with affordability, delivery capacity, technical considerations and benefits realisation. It will also strengthen the governance, assurance and performance disciplines that enable transparent decisions and timely course correction.


The Deputy Secretary also leads designated corporate stewardship functions, including legal, communications, ministerial and executive services, and will play an important role in shaping DGS's future operating model, building organisational capability and representing the department in whole-of-government strategy, reform and investment discussions.

 

About You


You are a highly credible enterprise executive who has helped a large, complex organisation determine its future direction and make difficult choices about priorities, sequencing, stewardship and performance. You bring more than functional expertise in strategy, digital, technology or transformation; you have operated across organisational boundaries and influenced decisions affecting multiple services, functions and stakeholder groups.


You have the judgement, presence and political acumen to become a trusted adviser to the Secretary and a respected peer to other Deputy Secretaries. You can bring clarity to ambiguity, frame genuine choices and constructively challenge established thinking while building trust and alignment across senior stakeholders.


You will bring meaningful experience setting portfolio direction and applying prioritisation, sequencing and investment discipline across services, products, programs or enterprise initiatives. You understand the distinction between delivering individual projects and stewarding an interconnected portfolio over time, including decisions about capacity, affordability and relative value.


You do not need to be a technologist, but you will be digitally literate and able to work credibly across product management, service delivery, operations, data and technology. Public sector experience and prior ministerial exposure is highly desirable. Above all, you will be an enterprise-minded, values-driven leader motivated by public value, integrity and responsible stewardship of public resources.
